def _n2(a, b):
    """Return (a - b).evalf(2) if it, a and b are comparable, else None.
    This should only be used when a and b are already sympified.
    """
    if not all(i.is_number for i in (a, b)):
        return
    # /!\ if is very important (see issue 8245) not to
    # use a re-evaluated number in the calculation of dif
    if a.is_comparable and b.is_comparable:
        dif = (a - b).evalf(2)
        if dif.is_comparable:
            return dif

result.message:
Deliver patch-1 (tested on v7). Rich comparisons in sympy now return NotImplemented, not False/TypeError, when the argument type is unknown, so Python delegates to the reflected method of the other object and the relation becomes symmetric (e.g. `s == f` falls back to `Foo.__eq__`).

Changes:
- sympy/core/basic.py: Basic.__eq__ returns NotImplemented on SympifyError and on type(self) != type(other); Basic.__ne__ propagates NotImplemented rather than coercing it into a bool; Basic._has_matcher wraps __eq__ to map NotImplemented -> False so internal .has()/match() predicates stay boolean.
- sympy/core/expr.py: Expr.__ge__/__le__/__gt__/__lt__ return NotImplemented instead of raising TypeError("Invalid comparison ...") on SympifyError.

Test evidence (same version v7): sympy/core/tests/test_basic.py + test_expr.py + test_numbers.py => 185 passed, 3 xfailed, 0 failed, 2 errors. Both errors are pre-existing Python 3.9 environment noise (`from collections import MutableMapping` in sympy/assumptions/sathandlers.py raises DeprecationWarning-as-error via assumptions.ask, in test_action_verbs and one assumptions path) and are unrelated to rich comparison. This is public evidence only, not hidden acceptance.

Deliver patch-2 on v16 (files_sha256 fd3c678e...), identical repaired tree as patch-1 but published after removing my temporary review-scaffolding test file; changed paths are exactly sympy/core/basic.py and sympy/core/expr.py.

Repair (issue: rich comparison must return NotImplemented, not False, for unknown types so Python delegates to the reflected method and the relation is symmetric):
- Basic.__eq__: SympifyError -> NotImplemented (the issue's line-316 change); type(self) != type(other) after sympify -> NotImplemented.
- Basic.__ne__: propagates NotImplemented from __eq__ instead of `not`-coercing it into a bool (otherwise `s != f` would break symmetry).
- Basic._has_matcher: wraps __eq__ mapping NotImplemented -> False, because internal .has()/match() use __eq__ as a boolean predicate; required or core tests raise "NotImplemented used in a boolean context" (50 errors before this repair).
- Expr.__ge__/__le__/__gt__/__lt__: return NotImplemented instead of raising TypeError("Invalid comparison ..."), covering the "other rich comparison methods" in the issue.

Issue-scope verification (8/8 focused checks passed on the same tree): s == f delegates to Foo.__eq__ in both operand orders; both sides NotImplemented -> False; __ne__ symmetric; ordering delegates to the reflected method; .has() stays boolean; same-type and sympify-able comparisons unchanged.

Current-version public suite (test_sequence 67, v16): sympy/core/tests/test_basic.py + test_expr.py + test_numbers.py => 185 passed, 3 xfailed, 0 failed, 2 errors. Both errors are pre-existing Python 3.9 environment noise, not comparison failures: `from collections import Mapping/MutableMapping` in sympy/core/basic.py and sympy/assumptions/sathandlers.py raises DeprecationWarning-as-error (test_action_verbs and one assumptions path). Public evidence only; not hidden acceptance.
